ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in circle $\odot O$, $AB$ is the diameter, and point $C$ is a point on the circle. The minor arc $AC$ is folded along chord $AC$ to intersect $AB$ at point $D$. Connect $CD$. If $\angle BAC=18^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle BDC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB$ is the diameter, \\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle BAC=18^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle B=90^\circ-\angle BAC=90^\circ-18^\circ=72^\circ$, \\
According to the property of reflection, \\
the inscribed angle corresponding to arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$ is $\angle B$, \\
the inscribed angle corresponding to arc $\overset{\frown}{ABC}$ is $\angle ADC$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADC+\angle B=180^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle ADC+\angle BDC=180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle BDC=\boxed{72^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle; A is on the left side of the circle, B is on the upper right side of the circle, and C is on the lower right side of the circle; line segment AB passes through the center O of the circle, indicating that AB is a diameter. AC and BC are connected. In the figure there is also an arc-shaped curve from A to C inside the circle passing through point D; point D is located on line AB, and CD is connected; this corresponds to the meaning of the problem that after folding the minor arc AC along chord AC, it intersects AB at D. Reasoning: Because AB is the diameter of the circle, by the theorem of the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter, ∠ACB=90°. It is known that ∠BAC=18°, therefore in triangle ABC, ∠ABC=90°-18°=72°. ∠ABC intercepts the arc AC in the original circle that does not contain B, so the measure of the original minor arc AC is 2×72°=144°. Folding along chord AC keeps the measure of the arc unchanged, therefore the measure of the folded arc ADC is also 144°. In the folded circle, ∠ADC intercepts the other complementary arc AC, whose measure is 360°-144°=216°, so ∠ADC=216°÷2=108°. From the figure it can be seen that A, D, B are collinear, and DA and DB are opposite rays, therefore ∠ADC and ∠BDC are supplementary, so ∠BDC=180°-108°=72°.
